description.narrative:
The Love Alliance, a new five-year programme (2021-2025), is based on an unwavering commitment to protecting, promoting and fulfilling sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) globally, unifying people who use drugs, sex workers and LGBTIQ+ movements, and amplifying the diversity of voices in these communities.
Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Love Alliance brings together national thought leaders GALZ, SANPUD and Sisonke, regional grantmakers UHAI EASHRI, AFE and ISDAO, with the global network of people living with HIV (GNP+) and the Netherlands-based administrative lead Aidsfonds.
Together, we advocate for adequate levels of funding and for taking truly human rights-based programmes to scale. We take this opportunity to prioritise and invest in challenging the structural barriers of underfunding, criminalisation and exclusion of us in all our diversity.

comment.narrative: There are not initial CSOs strengthened in order to set up a functional baseline. CSOs will be counted according to the capacity strengthening by taking part of the Love Alliance. South Africa has well-developed civil society and community-led organisations, with communities of sex workers and LGBTIQ+ communities displaying world-class organizing and advocacy. The country’s LGBTIQ+ movement has an estimated 10-15 organisations. Approximately 10% of the organisations are youth-led and 60% refer to women-led CSOs in the country. Despite a restrictive policy environment, sex workers are also well-organised. The community of people who use drugs, while more recent in their organizing, also serves as a regional leader.

A grantmaking system was established in the country and CSOs received grants to start implementation. A tailor-made capacity strengthening will take place on 2022, and therefore the results from the activities

South Africa has well-developed civil society and community-led organisations, with communities of sex workers and LGBTIQ+ communities displaying world-class organizing and advocacy. The country’s LGBTIQ+ movement has an estimated 10-15 organisations. Approximately 10% of the organisations are youth-led and 60% refer to women-led CSOs in the country. Despite a restrictive policy environment, sex workers are also well-organised. The community of people who use drugs, while more recent in their organizing, also serves as a regional leader.
Five (5) KP-led organizations have had their capacities on advocacy strengthened through a mix of trainings, inclusion in HLMs, linking and learning with other stakeholders.

The support from resource partners, and consequential growth of the Alliance partners has been a constant exercise during the first year. The joint work between Sisonke and Aidsfonds has resulted in a new management structure, 21 HR policies and job descriptions were developed for the new staff members. Additionally, Mainline helped to establish SANPUD’s strategic information position needed to fully enact its responsibility as a thought leader on drug-related issues within the Love Alliance. The CSOs Imvelo Hashtag in Esctourt, NNPL and Ubumbano in Newcastle have also increased their capacity through knowledge sharing, trainings to understand their role as a partner and to make the organisations more efficient in the services that they provide to their communities. Trainings on organisational policies, HR, project management, financial management, as well as SRHR, gender and sexuality, amongst other technical topics, led to internal analysis on governance and the importance of compliance with the Department of Social Development.

comment.narrative: Currently there is no functioning human rights accountability mechanism at the national level, and efforts to scale up community-led monitoring are underway, but focus on HIV-related services (not SRHR independently).

NAPs have openly challenged the Minister of Social Development on the criminalization approaches against pregnant women using drugs helping in bringing the potential consequences on public health and outreach to the table.

NAPs participated in the forum's meetings and District AIDS Council meetings fostering collaboration, accountability, and community building, leading to coordinated HIV/AIDS efforts, inclusion of the LGBTIQ+ community, increased transparency, and additional funding for domestic HIV programmes and initiatives.

Sisonke engages with Civil Society – Community Led Monitoring (CLM) Ad Hoc Committee, which measures successful implementation of AFSA as the new PR (primary recipient for GF/PEPFAR) in South Africa. Sisonke is working closely with them to ensure that capacitation and knowledge is shared amongst them. Under CLM, communities will have tools and techniques to collect and analyse their own data; they are able to increase domestic oversight and conduct evidence-based advocacy to improve services for HIV and related conditions.

Uthingo Network serves on the Provincial Victim Empowerment Forum (PVEP KZN) and the Provincial Task Team against Hate Crimes and Biases (PTT), both accountability structures. Through these platforms hate crime is addressed, and stakeholders are made aware of the challenges faced by the LGBTI+ community within several government departments, including local clinics, local police stations, home affairs, and tribal councils. This network actively follows up on hate crimes and reports these to the Provincial Task Team. The network also provides psychosocial support to families that have been affected by hate crimes. The responses by the Task Team to the cases that are shared are very limited.
3 community-based organisations use the results of monitoring hate crimes as input to leverage the efforts on accountability of the South African government (This is a 5-year target)
